title: Consensus
tagline: Three machines keep one log between them, so losing one loses nothing. What has to be true before a write is safe, and who is really in charge?

client.name: Client
client.brief: Sends writes and wants to know when one is truly saved.

application.name: Leader
application.brief: Takes writes, sends them to the followers, and decides when one is committed.

idp.name: Follower A
idp.brief: Keeps a copy of the log. Votes in elections.

mcp.name: Follower B
mcp.brief: Keeps a copy of the log. Votes in elections.

teaches: A write is safe once a majority has it on disk. Not when the leader has it, and not only when everyone does.
Terms settle who leads: a higher term always wins, and a leader that sees one steps down.
A node on the small side of a split must refuse, or the two sides will disagree.
All of this assumes nodes fail by stopping. A node that lies needs a different, costlier protocol.

glossary.means: More than half the nodes: two of three. Any two majorities share a node, which is why they can't disagree.
The point at which an entry will never be lost or changed, because a majority has stored it.
A numbered period with at most one leader. Every message carries its term.
A follower accepts a new entry only if the entry before it matches its own log.
Two sides of a broken network each accepting writes, producing two histories.
A node that sends wrong or conflicting messages, as opposed to one that stops.
